qs.q: A 40-year-old man presents with vertigo brought on by changing head positions, lasting less than a minute. Dix-Hallpike maneuver elicits rotary nystagmus and delayed onset vertigo. What is the pathological mechanism?
o: Increased endolymph volume causing dilation of the membranous semicircular duct.
Free-floating otoconia displaced into the posterior semicircular canal (canalithiasis).
Viral reactivation leading to inflammation of the vestibular nerve.
Perilymph leakage through a fistula at the oval window.
Ischemic reduction of blood flow to the brainstem vestibular nuclei.
qs.e: BPPV is caused by canalithiasis where otoconia migrate into the semicircular canal.

qs.q: A 55-year-old man presents with episodic vertigo, fluctuating low-frequency hearing loss, tinnitus, and a sensation of fullness in the right ear. Which histopathological finding characterizes this condition?
o: Bony fixation of the stapes footplate preventing its movement.
Atrophic loss of hair cells within the organ of Corti.
Degeneration of the myelin sheath surrounding the main vestibular nerve.
Dilatation of the endolymphatic spaces producing inner‑ear hydrops.
Suppurative infection involving the mastoid air cell system.
qs.e: Meniere disease is histologically defined by endolymphatic hydrops within the inner ear.

qs.q: A 45-year-old man presents with vertigo and impaired perception of rotational head movements during rapid turns. Which specific structure within the vestibular apparatus contains the receptor cells that detect this form of acceleration?
qs.e: The semicircular canals detect angular acceleration via ampullae containing hair cells that respond to endolymph movement during rotation. The macula of the saccule and utricle are instead involved in detecting linear acceleration and gravity.

qs.q: A patient with severe motion sickness requires a medication that controls vertigo by inhibiting signals from the internal ear to the vomiting center. Which drug is appropriate for this indication?
qs.e: Promethazine acts on firing pathways from the internal ear to the vomiting center to treat motion sickness. Cyproheptadine is used to increase appetite rather than treat motion sickness.
